description_en: Sarasvatī Nani (courtyard) is located to the north of Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra which is also known as Kvā Bāhāḥ or Golden Temple. The one-story temple in the courtyard's center holds a metal statue of Dharmacakra Mañjuśrī in its sanctum. Mañjunātha is a form of Mañjuśrī which is shown with three faces and six arms (Bhattacharyya1987, 81). Buddhists worship the deity as Mañjuśrī or Mañjunātha, whereas Hindus worship the deity as Sarasvatī. Local residents refer to the temple with the names of both deities (Mañjuśrī and Sarasvatī), although the courtyard is generelly known as Sarasvatī Nani. A legend tells that there once was an Ashoka tree where the temple stands today. A flash of lightning struck the tree causing it to wither and dry out. A Śākya from Kvāḥ Bāhāḥ used the tree trunk to carve a statue of Mañjuśrī and constructed the temple where the tree once stood. The original wooden statue was stolen around five decades ago. Alongside the new statue of Mañjuśrī, one can also find statues of Gaṇeśa and Bhairava.The temple has an open colonnaded circumambulatory with three bays on each side. The door is decorated with carvings of Buddhist deities and floral patterns and a carved aedicule is embedded in the masonry wall. The first floor walls have three small latticed windows on each side. The roof is covered with copper sheets and surmounted by a gilt pinnacle. The corner struts are carved and the rest of them are plain. The eaves of the roof are decorated with metal frills and hanging wind chimes. Twośikharakuṭa caityashave been built in the courtyard, one in front of the temple (east) and the other one to the north of the temple. A shrine to Śākyamuni Buddha has been erected to the south of the temple. It is covered with a copper roof supported by iron posts. The courtyard has a small passage at its northeast corner that leads to Ilā Nani (the western courtyard).Three inscriptions are attached to the southern, western and northern walls. The oldest inscription attests to the temple's renovation in 1724 CE. Two inscriptions,  dated NS 845 and 857, mention to first invoke Mañjunātha before praying to Sarasvatī. A document concerning land transfers, dated NS 833 (1713 CE), mentions Sarasvatī Nani (S.RājavaṃśīVS 2042, 21). The temple was renovated in 2002.
description_ne: यस चतुष्कोणाकार ननिको केन्द्रभागमा मञ्जुश्रीको एक तले मन्दिर रहेको छ । नेवार समुदायभित्र हिन्दूमार्गीले विद्याकी देवीका रूपमा सरस्वतीलाई पूज्ने गर्छन् भने बौद्धमार्गीले मञ्जुश्रीलाई पुज्दछन् । मञ्जुश्री मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरी राखिएको नेसं ८४५ को अभिलेख सरस्वतीको स्तुतिबाट प्रारम्भ गरिएको छ । यसबाट उत्तर मध्यकालमा विद्यादाता मञ्जुश्री र सरस्वतीलाई एकै मानिने चलन थियो कि भन्ने अनुमान हुन्छ । मञ्जुश्रीको मन्दिर भएको ननिलाई सरस्वती ननि भनिएबाट पनि यस कुरामा बल पुग्दछ । नेसं ८३३को भूमिसम्बन्धि तमसूक ताडपत्रमा पनि 'सरस्वती ननि' नामोल्लेख छ (RājavaṃśīVS 2042, 21) । यसबाट उत्तरमध्यकालदेखि नै यो स्थानलाई सरस्वती ननि भनिदै आएको बुझिन्छ । गर्भगृहमा रहेको मञ्जुश्रीले दुई हातका हत्केलालाई आपसमा जोडी धर्मचक्र मुद्रामा राखेका छन् । यस विशेषताका आधारमा यो मूर्तिलाई धर्मचक्र मञ्जुश्री भन्ने गरिएको छ । पहिला यस मन्दिरमा रहेको मञ्जुश्रीको काठको मूर्ति चोरी भएपछि अहिले रहेको धातुको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको हो । मञ्जुश्रीका साथै गर्भगृहभित्र गणेश र भैरवको मूर्ति पनि रहेका छन् । ननिमा मन्दिरका अलावा शाक्यमुनि बुद्धको मूर्ति र दुईवटा शिखरकूट चैत्य पनि रहेका छन् ।यस मन्दिरको स्थापनाबारे जानकारी दिने सामग्री प्राप्त भएको छैन। मन्दिरमा पाइएको सबैभन्दा पुरानो अभिलेख सन् १७२४ को हो । उक्त साल मन्दिरको जीर्णोद्धार गरिएको थियो । मन्दिरको पछिल्लो जीर्णोद्धार विसं २०५९ सालमा भएको थियो । स्थानीय वासिन्दाले बताएको मन्दिर निर्माणसँग सम्बन्धित लोकोक्ति अनुसार रुद्रवर्ण महाविहार (क्वाःबाहाः) को उत्तरतिर पर्ने यो ननिमा पहिला एउटा अशोक वृक्ष थियो । चट्याङमा परी त्यो वृक्ष सुकेर गयो। पछि क्वाःबाहाःका एक शाक्यले त्यो वृक्ष रहेकै स्थानमा सोही वृक्षको सदुपयोग गरी मन्दिर र मञ्जुश्रीको मूर्ति निर्माण गरे ।उपत्यकाका अन्य सरस्वती र मञ्जुश्री मन्दिरमा जस्तै यहाँ पनि श्रीपञ्चमी (माघ शुक्ल पञ्चमी) का दिन श्रद्धालुहरूको भीड लाग्ने गर्दछ । सो दिन रातभर जाग्राम वस्ने, तुतः पाठ गर्ने, दीप बाल्ने एवं आफ्नो पेशासँग सम्बन्धित वस्तु मूर्तिमा छुवाई ढोग्ने परम्परा छ । यसै ननिमा बस्ने याकःछेँ खलः भनिने शाक्य खलकले एक वर्षमा क्रमश पालो फेर्दै मन्दिरमा नित्य पूजा सम्पन्न गर्दै आएका छन् (Śākya2013: 135) ।

historical_events.event_description: Jñānaśrī, Dharmamuni, Dhanasiṃha Jayasiṃ, Pariṣadeva, Kutusiṃha, Mahīndra, Maṇirāja and others renovated the temple.

Samvarasiṃ and Maṇirāja offered flags, a golden pinnacle and garlands in memory of their father Dharmasiṃha. They also established a statue of Prajñāpāramitā in memory of their mothers Lakṣmī and Lakṣavatī. Rakṣasiṃ, Guṇākarasiṃ, Jñānīkarasiṃ, Lakṣavatī, Vasundharā, Apsarā, Sūryavatī and other family members are also mentioned.

Most of the letters on the inscription are effaced. The writing appears to mention a land donation and offers regulations as to how to use its income to organise worship rituals. However, it is not clear whether this concerns thecaityaor the temple.
Harṣamāna and Lakṣmīmāyā donated the oil lamp balustrade that surrounds the Śikharakūṭacaitya(LAL0108-002).
Yajñaratna donated the oil lamp balustrade that surrounds the Śikharakūṭacaitya(LAL0108-004).
Members of Yākaḥ Chẽ Khalaḥ collected donations and renovated the temple. The flags, banners and eaves board were renewed as well.
